findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and will raise on render
findings.body: The if/else block is terminated with `<%- end if %>`. `end if` is a syntax error in Ruby (`if` used as a modifier with no condition), so compiling this template raises a SyntaxError and the `embed#best` action will 500 whenever a topic exists. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: request.referer interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` injects an attacker-controlled HTTP header directly into a JS string literal with no escaping. A referer containing a single quote (e.g. `http://x'+alert(1)+'`) breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the Discourse origin, which also has the session cookie available. Escape with `j`/`javascript_escape` (or build the target origin from scheme+host only).

findings.title: Raw rendering of posts whose cooked HTML is unsanitized remote content
findings.body: `raw post.cooked` is emitted in the embed view, while `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html` (posts imported from RSS/readability). That means arbitrary HTML/JS pulled from a third-party feed is stored as `cooked` and rendered unsanitized inside a page on the forum's own origin. The imported HTML should be sanitized (whitelist tags/attributes) before being stored or rendered.

findings.title: `force: true` in create_table will silently drop an existing table
findings.body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If the migration is ever re-run (or the table exists for any reason), all topic_embeds rows are destroyed without warning. Remove `force: true` from migrations.

findings.title: Editing an already-released migration to add `force: true` risks dropping top_topics
findings.body: This changes an existing migration (which may already have run on deployed sites) to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, i.e. drop-then-create. Any environment that re-runs or re-plays migrations loses the table and its data. Migrations should be immutable once shipped, and `force: true` should not be used here.

findings.title: poll_feed crashes when feed items have no `content`
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description`, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the job raises NoMethodError; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the whole polling run is lost. Also `String#scrub` requires Ruby >= 2.1. Fall back to `description`/`content_encoded` and guard against nil.

findings.title: `open` used without requiring open-uri in topic_embed.rb
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` but this file only requires nokogiri and ruby-readability. open-uri is only required in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, so when `import_remote` is reached via TopicRetriever/RetrieveTopic without PollFeed having been loaded, `open` falls back to Kernel#open and will fail (or behave unexpectedly) on an http URL. Add `require 'open-uri'` here.

findings.title: open-uri `open` on a URL permits pipe/file access and unbounded fetch
findings.body: `open(url)` with Kernel#open semantics treats a string starting with `|` as a shell command and non-http strings as local file paths. Although TopicRetriever checks the host, `import_remote` is also called directly (disqus.thor, and `poll_feed` uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`), so a crafted feed URL setting can read local files or run commands. Use an explicit HTTP fetch (e.g. `URI.parse(url).open` after validating scheme) and bound the response size.

findings.title: Weak postMessage origin check on the host page
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a *substring* of the configured discourse URL (e.g. `http://disc` or a prefix match), and it does not anchor at position 0. Any page able to postMessage can then resize the iframe. Compare the origin exactly against the origin component of discourseUrl.

findings.title: `import` mutates the caller's contents string
findings.body: `contents << "...imported from..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller. Callers that reuse or cache that string (and frozen-literal strings) will see corruption / RuntimeError. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

findings.title: Missing embed_url raises ParameterMissing producing a 500 rather than a 400/404
findings.body: `params.require(:embed_url)` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, which is not rescued here; unless the app has a global handler this surfaces as a 500 error with a backtrace rather than a clean 400. The accompanying spec only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it passes either way.

findings.title: Dead code: feed_key is computed but never used
findings.body: `feed_key` builds a redis key for feed modification tracking but nothing reads or writes it, so the feed is re-parsed and re-imported in full every hour with no conditional-GET/ETag handling. Either implement the caching or drop the method.
